# kazu (数)

`kazu` is the game-engine suite's tiny standard library for repeated numeric operations. It is ESM, dependency-free, headless, and contains no ambient randomness.

```js
import { clamp01, median, mulberry32 } from 'kazu';

const rng = mulberry32(42);
const bounded = clamp01(rng());
const center = median([1, 9, 3, 5]); // 4
```

## API

- `SCHEMA_VERSION`
- `clamp(x, lo, hi)`, `clamp01(x)`, `clampSym(x, a)`
- `lerp(a, b, t)`, `round(x, digits)`
- `mulberry32(seed)`, `rngFrom(seed)`
- `median(arr)`
- `bench(fn, { warmup, rounds, stat: 'min' | 'median' })`

`lerp` permits extrapolation. `round` requires an explicit digit position. `median` copies before sorting and throws `RangeError` for an empty input. `bench` requires an explicit `stat`; it returns `{ stat, value, samples }` in milliseconds. Tests may additionally pass a `clock` function.

## Decisions from the existing copies

| Function | Variants found in the workspace | Canonical decision and reason |
|---|---|---|
| `clamp` / `clamp01` | Most use `(x, lo, hi)` comparisons; a minority use `(lo, hi, value)`, default bounds, `Math.min/Math.max`, or map non-finite values to zero. | `(x, lo, hi)` with comparisons matches the clear majority. `NaN` passes through, while infinities clamp to finite bounds. Bounds are not reordered. |
| `clampSym` | Existing music copies hard-code `[-1, 1]`. | Accept magnitude `a`, as required, and use `Math.abs(a)` so the interval stays symmetric even when its sign is accidental. |
| `lerp` | Nearly all use `(a, b, t)`; a few integration helpers clamp `t`. | Do not clamp `t`: this preserves the majority behavior and useful extrapolation. |
| `round` | Digit defaults vary (2/3/4/6/9); implementations differ on non-finite values and negative zero. | Require `digits` and use the majority scale/round/unscale formula. `NaN` propagates, infinity stays infinite, and negative digits are supported. |
| `mulberry32` | Cosmetic differences use `| 0` or `>>> 0`; the common state transition and output divisor are the same. One tetsugo test uses another algebraic form. | Preserve the dominant transition byte-for-byte in operation order and divide by `2^32`, producing `[0, 1)`. |
| `rngFrom` | Most copies are the music-engine golden-ratio-scrambled LCG; tetsugo test helpers wrap `mulberry32` and sometimes hash strings. | Preserve the numeric-seed LCG majority, including historical division by `0xffffffff`. Use `mulberry32` when a strict `[0, 1)` range is required. |
| `median` | Empty input returns `0`, `null`, or implicit `undefined`; most even-length versions average, while some benchmarks select the upper middle. Some sort the caller's array. | Require non-empty input, copy it, and average the middle pair. `NaN` explicitly propagates; infinities sort normally. A `RangeError` makes missing samples visible. |
| `bench` | Existing scripts differ in clocks, batching, return units, and choose min or median implicitly. | One call per round, milliseconds, returned samples, and a mandatory statistic. No contextual default is smuggled into the shared library. |

Run `node --test`.
